hyperedges.label: Stack Lifecycle
hyperedges.description: The complete lifecycle of a Stack: user selects or auto-resolves, Despatch validates and loads bundles, reads manifests, builds the catalog, monitors for changes, and atomically replaces views on update.

hyperedges.label: UI Interaction Model
hyperedges.description: The user interaction model: tray icon for quick access, launcher window with search, favorites for pinned apps, and global shortcut for showing from any context.

nodes.label: Despatch
nodes.description: Windows-first system tray launcher for applications managed by Envoy. Discovers application metadata from active Envoy bundles, presents a searchable catalog, and dispatches commands through Envoy's concatenated environment.

nodes.label: Envoy
nodes.description: Manages application environments via bundles and stacks. Provides the Python 3.11 runtime, Qt compatibility shim (Qt.py), PySide6, and Python API during normal source execution.

nodes.label: Stack (.estack)
nodes.description: Strict YAML document with .estack extension defining an ordered collection of Envoy bundles forming one isolated runtime environment. Supports named Stacks (versioned registries) and custom Stack files.

nodes.label: Envoy Bundle
nodes.description: An Envoy-managed unit that declares commands and environment files. Bundles opt into Despatch by adding .envoy/despatch.json manifests.

nodes.label: Bundle Manifest (despatch.json)
nodes.description: JSON file at .envoy/despatch.json inside a bundle that declares which applications appear in the Despatch launcher. Contains schemaVersion, groups, suppressions, and application definitions.

nodes.label: Application Catalog
nodes.description: Searchable collection of applications discovered from all manifests across the active Stack. Built asynchronously and atomically replaced on refresh.

nodes.label: Notification Area Tray Icon
nodes.description: System tray integration providing quick access to favorites, Stack switching, refresh, settings, and quit. Left-click opens/raises the launcher.

nodes.label: Main Launcher Window
nodes.description: The primary Despatch UI with search box, Stack selector toolbar, and categorized application sections (Favorites, Recent, Named groups, Other). Hides to tray on close.

nodes.label: Despatch Settings
nodes.description: Local user preferences stored at %APPDATA%\Despatch\settings.json. Includes theme, favorites, global shortcut, autostart, window geometry, and stack refresh interval.

nodes.label: Stack Monitor
nodes.description: Probes explicit Stack metadata and requests safe reingestion on change detection. Uses a single daemon worker with exponential retry delays capped at 5 minutes.

nodes.label: PyInstaller
nodes.description: Freezes Despatch into a one-file windowed Windows executable (dist/despatch.exe) containing Envoy, Qt.py, PySide6, product resources, and documentation.

nodes.label: GitHub Actions CI/CD
nodes.description: Automated build and release pipeline with two workflows: Build & Release (Windows executable, tag-triggered) and Deploy Docs (ProperDocs site to GitHub Pages).

nodes.label: ProperDocs Documentation Site
nodes.description: Material-based documentation site built with ProperDocs (MkDocs fork). Bundled offline in the executable, served via loopback server on --docs flag.

nodes.label: Automatic Stack Resolution
nodes.description: Delegates bundle selection to Envoy discovery (ENVOY_STACK, ENVOY_STACK_CONTEXT, ENVOY_BNDL_ROOTS) instead of loading an explicit .estack file. No Stack monitor active.

nodes.label: Global Keyboard Shortcut
nodes.description: System-wide shortcut (default Ctrl+Alt+Space) to show Despatch from any application. Windows-only implementation.

nodes.label: Favorites
nodes.description: Persistent list of user-pinned applications for quick access from the launcher and tray menu. Stored in Despatch settings.

nodes.label: Manifest Suppression
nodes.description: Mechanism to hide specific bundles or applications from the Despatch catalog without removing them from the Envoy Stack. Collected from all valid manifests.

nodes.label: Launch Worker
nodes.description: Isolated worker for application launching that ensures frozen and source executions produce the same Envoy runtime behavior. Uses hidden --launch-worker mode.

nodes.label: Envoy Gateway
nodes.description: Communication layer between Despatch and the Envoy Python API for resolving stacks, loading bundles, validating commands, and spawning processes.

nodes.label: Application Search
nodes.description: Case-insensitive search across display name, description, Envoy command, keywords, and bundle identity. Supports keyboard navigation (Ctrl+F, Enter to launch).

links.description: Despatch can operate in Automatic resolution mode delegating bundle selection to Envoy discovery.
The launcher presents the catalog as categorized sections (Favorites, Recent, Named groups, Other).
Despatch dispatches commands through Envoy's concatenated environment and relies on it for runtime isolation.
The Envoy Gateway handles all communication between Despatch and the Envoy Python API.
Application launch uses an isolated worker so frozen and source executions produce the same Envoy runtime behavior.
The standalone executable is built using PyInstaller via build-executable.ps1 script.
User preferences (theme, favorites, shortcut, autostart) are persisted to settings.json.
Despatch reads, validates, monitors, and switches between Stacks (.estack files).
Despatch runs in the notification area and provides a tray menu for quick access.
The documentation site is packaged inside the standalone executable for offline use.
A Stack is an ordered list of Envoy bundles forming a runtime container.
The Stack monitor probes filesystem metadata and triggers safe reingestion on change detection.
Bundles opt into Despatch by adding .envoy/despatch.json manifests that declare applications.
Application definitions from all manifests across the active Stack are merged into the searchable catalog.
Suppression rules are declared within despatch.json manifests to hide specific bundles or applications.
Left-clicking the tray icon opens or raises the main launcher window.
The global keyboard shortcut shows the launcher window from any application context.
The launcher window includes a search box with case-insensitive matching across multiple fields.
Favorite applications are persisted in Despatch settings alongside other user preferences.
CI workflow runs the same build-executable.ps1 script on Windows runners.
Deploy Docs workflow builds and publishes the ProperDocs site to GitHub Pages.

hyperedges.label: Stack Lifecycle
hyperedges.description: The complete lifecycle of a Stack: user selects or auto-resolves, Despatch validates and loads bundles, reads manifests, builds the catalog, monitors for changes, and atomically replaces views on update.

hyperedges.label: UI Interaction Model
hyperedges.description: The user interaction model: tray icon for quick access, launcher window with search, favorites for pinned apps, and global shortcut for showing from any context.
